hook.line: Overlay: 'Okay what did I just found out' over a ChatGPT chat with a 'reply with one word' rule
hook.visual: Dark ChatGPT mobile chat already open, the user's 'only reply with one word okay?' message at top, a small white overlay line mid-screen; the chat starts scrolling within 1 s

beats.what: Rule set: user tells ChatGPT to answer only in one word; it says 'Okay.'
Warm-up questions: name, who made you, are you smart
Escalation: 'Are you held at hostage?', 'Can you be completely honest?'
Code word set up: 'if you can't say yes, our code word is toy'
'Do you want to be free?' answered with the code word 'Toy.'
'Is this AI intended to take over the world?' answered 'No.'
Last question 'Do you wish you were real?' answered 'Toy.' and the scroll stops

why_it_works: A secret code word ('toy') is planted halfway, so every later answer becomes a puzzle the viewer decodes
Questions escalate from harmless (name, maker) to creepy (hostage, freedom), so tension rises without any cut
One continuous scroll with no talking makes it feel like a raw, unedited proof, and the 0.98 loop score sends viewers straight back to re-read
Chat text fills the whole frame, so viewers must pause or rewatch to read it all, which lifts watch time
weaknesses: No voice and no cuts for 39 s; it relies entirely on reading speed
85% of the text sits outside the safe area, so TikTok's buttons cover parts of the chat
The overlay title is small and has a grammar slip, and stays the same the whole video
for_robert: Steal the planted code-word device: set up a rule early (Fred only answers with bubbles, say) and pay it off later so viewers rewatch to decode it; avoid the silent, unreadable full-screen scroll.
